newsitem.title: USA: Washington Mutual, Great Western to merge.
newsitem.headline: Washington Mutual, Great Western to merge.

text.p: Washington Mutual Savings Bank and Great Western Financial Corp announced Thursday an agreement to merge in a stock swap valued at $6.6 billion.
Under terms of the agreement, Washington Mutual will exchange 0.9 share for each outstanding Great Western share in a tax-free swap.
Great Western is the target of a hostile takeover bid by A.H. Ahmanson and Co. Ahmanson has proposed a stock swap worth about $6.2 billion.

Under the Washington Mutual-Great Western pact, each share of Great Western 8.30 percent cumulative preferred stock would be converted into one share of a new series of Washington Mutual preferred stock with essentially the same terms.
Also, four Great Western directors would be added to Washington Mutual's board.
Based on 1996 results, the combined companies would have assets of $87.4 billion and deposits of $52.7 billion, the companies said.

The merger would rank Washington Mutual third in deposits in the state of California and give it entry into the state of Florida, where Great Western had $7.1 billion in deposits at the end of 1996, they said.
If the merger is terminated under certain circumstances, Great Western will pay Washington Mutual $75 million plus documented expenses not exceeding $20 million, the companies said.
As part of the transaction, Washington Mutual will incur a pre-tax charge of $440 million -- $278 million net after taxes -- including an addition to loan-loss reserves of $100 million.
Total pre-tax expense reductions, on a combined basis, are expected to total $208 million in 1998 and $340 million in 1999, the companies said.
